title: The segment group API, model fields and Terraform resource

prose.text: This subject covers the segment group endpoints, model fields and the Terraform resource and data source.

prose.label: Model fields.
prose.text: {{go-model-flags}} {{config-space-values}} What configSpace means is open {{gap:config-space-meaning}}. What the keepalive field does is open {{gap:tcp-keep-alive-enabled-effect}}, and its type differs between the spec and the Go model {{divergence:tcp-keep-alive-enabled-type-differs}}. What skipDetailedAppInfo does is open {{gap:skip-detailed-app-info-effect}}.

prose.label: Terraform.
prose.text: {{tf-resource-schema}} {{tf-import}} {{tf-data-source-outputs}} The data source docs list two attributes the schema lacks {{divergence:tf-data-source-docs-vs-schema}}. Provider defects around these objects are in [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects]] and [[zpa.terraform.data-source-selection]].

checks.do: Which update version the tool in use calls, since the v1 and v2 bodies differ.
Whether enabled and policyMigrated are written explicitly, since the Go model never omits them.
Whether Terraform state for applications reflects the group's real membership, which the resource reads back but writes as IDs only.

endpoints.statement: The segment group API lists and creates at `/mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/segmentGroup`, gets, updates and deletes at `.../segmentGroup/{segmentGroupId}`, and has a separate v2 update at `/mgmtconfig/v2/.../segmentGroup/{segmentGroupId}`.

expect.description: Gets all configured Segment Groups for the specified customer.
Adds a new Segment Group for the specified customer.
Gets the Segment Group details for the specified ID.
Updates the Segment Group for the specified ID.
Deletes the Segment Group for the specified ID.

v2-body-differs.statement: The v1 segment group body has `policyMigrated`, `applicationNames` and `sharedMicrotenantIds`, while the v2 update body has `addedApps` and `deletedApps` instead.

sdks-expose-both-updates.statement: The Go SDK exposes `Update` (v1 path) and `UpdateV2` (v2 path), and the Python SDK exposes `update_group` and `update_group_v2` against the v1 and v2 base endpoints.

tf-update-uses-v2.conditions: Changed upstream in v4.4.14 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "The Terraform `zpa_segment_group` resource updates through `segmentgroup.UpdateV2`."

go-model-flags.statement: The Go segment group model tags `enabled` and `policyMigrated` without omitempty, so false is always sent.

config-space-values.statement: The API field `configSpace` on a segment group takes `DEFAULT` or `SIEM`.

tf-resource-schema.statement: The Terraform resource takes a required `name` and optional `description`, `enabled`, `microtenant_id` and an `applications` list of objects with a single `id` attribute; an `enabled` left out is sent as false. Before v4.4.14 only each application's ID was sent on every write; v4.4.14 deprecates `applications`, sends the application IDs only on create, never sends them on update, and rejects adding or removing applications on an existing group at plan time (#695).

tf-import.statement: A segment group can be imported into Terraform by ID or by name.

quotes: **segment_group** can be imported by using `<SEGMENT GROUP ID>` or `<SEGMENT GROUP NAME>` as the import ID.

tf-data-source-outputs.statement: The Terraform data source schema looks a group up by `id` or `name`, both optional, and exports `config_space`, the microtenant fields and a computed `applications` block.
tf-data-source-outputs.conditions: Statement changed from the docs' outputs: the schema has no policy_migrated or tcp_keep_alive_enabled and makes name optional, so the claim now states the schema and the docs' extra attributes are the tf-data-source-docs-vs-schema divergence.

tcp-keep-alive-enabled-type-differs.summary: The API spec types a segment group's `tcpKeepAliveEnabled` as an integer while the Go model types it as a string.

positions.says: The API spec types tcpKeepAliveEnabled as a 32-bit integer.
The Go model types tcpKeepAliveEnabled as a string.

tcp-keep-alive-enabled-type-differs.impact: A body written from the spec may send an integer where the SDK sends a string; the literal the service accepts is not shown by these sources.

tf-data-source-docs-vs-schema.summary: The zpa_segment_group data source docs list name as required and export policy_migrated and tcp_keep_alive_enabled, but the schema makes name optional and has neither attribute.

positions.says: The data source docs list name under Required and policy_migrated and tcp_keep_alive_enabled under Read-Only.

quotes: `name` - (Required) The name of the segment group to be exported.

positions.says: The data source schema declares name optional, and its top level ends at the microtenant fields with no policy_migrated or tcp_keep_alive_enabled attribute; Read sets neither.

tf-data-source-docs-vs-schema.impact: Referencing data.zpa_segment_group.<name>.policy_migrated or .tcp_keep_alive_enabled fails as an unsupported attribute; read those fields from the API or the SDK instead. Omitting name passes validation, and a lookup then needs id.

v2-update-differences.title: What the v2 segment group update changes behaviorally, and whether it is the preferred form
v2-update-differences.detail: Both SDK update bodies are built the same way and the spec shows different body fields, but the behavioral difference in field handling, application association writes and validation is not stated. Unverified legacy statement: the v2 update endpoint is the current-preferred form. Compare v1 and v2 update results for one group.

tcp-keep-alive-enabled-effect.title: What tcpKeepAliveEnabled on a segment group changes and how it relates to the segment-level setting
tcp-keep-alive-enabled-effect.blocks: saying whether the group setting overrides segment keepalive
tcp-keep-alive-enabled-effect.detail: No captured source describes the group-level TCP keepalive effect for brokered sessions, nor whether it overrides or is overridden by the application segment's TCP Keepalive setting. Unverified legacy statement: presence or absence of the field controls TCP keepalive behavior.

config-space-meaning.title: When a segment group's configSpace is anything other than DEFAULT
config-space-meaning.detail: The spec enumerates DEFAULT and SIEM. Unverified legacy statement: configSpace is typically DEFAULT and is not user-settable in standard configurations; the legacy reference also treats microtenantName as read-only and populated by the API when microtenantId is set. Read groups from a tenant with SIEM configuration.

skip-detailed-app-info-effect.title: Whether skipDetailedAppInfo is a request-side toggle or a stored attribute of a segment group
skip-detailed-app-info-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Python segment group model carries skip_detailed_app_info (wire key skipDetailedAppInfo) and round-trips it through request_format(), but the service layer does no special handling, so whether it suppresses the detailed application inflation in a response or is a stored attribute cannot be told from the SDK source. Needs an API reference or a lab test.
